title: CFR on Kuhn poker
brief: Enumerate Kuhn poker's information sets, compute exact best responses and exploitability, then run counterfactual regret minimization and check the average strategy against the game value of -1/18.
hints: regret_matching clips at zero with np.maximum, divides by the sum, and returns np.full(n, 1/n) when the sum is zero.

A best response picks one action per information set. Fix your card, carry one weight per opponent card, and take max(...) over your own actions outside the sum over opponent cards. A max inside each deal lets you see the opponent's card.
Exploitability is (BR_1 - v_1) + (BR_2 - v_2), and v_2 = -v_1 in a zero-sum game. It is 0 at an equilibrium.

Counterfactual regret multiplies by the opponent's reach (the other player's entry of the reach vector, with the deal's 1/6), not the acting player's. The strategy sum is the opposite: multiply by the acting player's own reach.
Compute every information set's regret-matching strategy before the walk, so all six deals use the strategies from the start of the iteration.
cfr_kuhn returns the average strategy, strategy_sum[k] / strategy_sum[k].sum(). The current strategy keeps jumping and does not converge.
